title: Cottongrove kiosk inventory integration - raw field notes
content:
Meeting: Cottongrove pilot kickoff (video) - 2025-02-17
Attendees: Samira (RSE), Noah (SE), Riley (Customer eng), Priya (Cottongrove infra), Marco (store ops)

Summary: quick intro + scope. Customer has 120 retail kiosks (model year 2019) with local Android boxes (4GB RAM, eMMC), intermittent LTE backhaul (10-30% of stores), and wired broadband otherwise. Goal: local inference fallback + cloud-hosted primary to reduce latency for checkout suggestions and barcode OCR post-processing.

Primary success metrics (customer):
- 95th percentile inference latency < 250ms for suggestion endpoint (local preferred)
- Token cost targets: keep cloud calls < 12% of interactions in steady state
- Offline tolerance: degrade gracefully to cached heuristics if no connectivity > 30s

Tech constraints / gotchas noted:
- Kiosk hardware cannot run current full float 7B model (RAM + storage insufficient). Need <1.5GB quantized variant; test int8/4-bit on Android NNAPI or via bundled microservice.
- eMMC I/O is slow; startup stall observed when model file cold-loaded -> warm model cache strategy required (preload during idle).
- Per-store network NAT mapping prevents stable callback webhooks; prefer polling or edge-mq with TLS outgoing only.
- PCI card-reader is serial-over-USB and blocks main thread occasionally; infer calls must be non-blocking and queued.
- Local disk writes limited; avoid large local logs. Use batched telemetry uploads during off-peak.

Proposed architecture sketch (notes to self):
1) Lightweight edge adapter (docker/shim) on kiosk that:
   - accepts POS input events (small JSON)
   - maintains local LRU KV cache for frequent SKU prompts
   - routes to local best-effort runtime if quantized model present
   - falls back to Redwood hosted API if no model or cold start + caches result
2) Model packaging: deliver a 4-bit quantized distilled suggestion model + small OCR postproc weights. Provide a size-optimized tar.gz with checksums and minimal runtime (python-free, native binary where possible).
3) Warm startup: updater job downloads model on idle windows (2-4am local) and verifies sha256. If insufficient disk, keep single-model resident per device.
4) Telemetry: only counters + sampled token cost traces; flush every 15 minutes over TLS to central endpoint.

Preliminary config suggestions for Redwood runtime:
- Use prefix caching for SKU prompts (cache key: store_id|sku|context-v2). TTL 1h, max 5000 entries.
- Batched local inference: group rapid POS events within 40ms window to utilize batching without visible latency.
- Graceful fallback policy: local->dedicated-region->hosted with rate limit 5 rps per store to hosted fallback to respect cost target.

Action items / next steps (owner):
- Samira: prototype lightweight adapter binary (Go) skeleton; initial message formats + test harness by 2025-02-25.
- Noah: run feasibility on 4-bit quantized candidate (distilled-2B->int4) on Android box emulator; perf numbers by 2025-02-24.
- Riley: share sample POS event logs + network diagnostics from 10 representative kiosks (needed: bandwidth histogram, NAT type) by 2025-02-21.
- Priya (Cottongrove): confirm maintenance window preference for model downloads (proposed 02:00-05:00 local).

Open questions / risks:
- Can we legally store any PII in local caches? Need legal check (likely no). Marked for security review.
- Edge binary dependencies: cross-compile matrix for Android x86 vs armv7/arm64; may need separate builds.
- Fallback cost: customer wants <12% cloud calls, but initial rollout may spike; propose canary with 5 stores first and budget guardrails.

Notes to self (random):
- Try embedding small sample of SKU embeddings for rerank on-device (cheap dot-products) instead of full gen when net is down.
- Consider tiny rule-engine fallback for promotions (simple if SKU in promo-list -> suggestion).
- Keep instrumentation IDs stable for ability to tie back to token billing.

Call cadence: weekly sync for first 6 weeks, ad-hoc for rollout days. Next meeting scheduled 2025-02-24 10:00 PST (invite sent).

Appendix: sample POS event (prototype format)
{
  "store_id": "CG-178",
  "txn_id": "20250217-98b2",
  "line_items": [{"sku":"CG-1492","qty":1}],
  "context": {"time_of_day":"evening","weather":"rain"}
}

(keep this doc messy — will formalize into confluence SE-1297 once initial data flows).
